title: South Carolina's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: South Carolina's 4th Congressional District, covering most of Greenville and Spartanburg counties in the Upstate region, will hold a general election on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Republican William Timmons, first elected in 2018, is seeking a fifth term after pledging this would be his last campaign. He defeated two primary challengers in the June 9 Republican primary with nearly 66% of the vote. The Democratic nominee is Courtney McClain, a 25-year-old civil rights activist who advanced uncontested from her primary. Libertarian candidate Jessica Ethridge is also on the ballot. Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Republican, and Timmons was endorsed by President Donald Trump in the primary.
polling_note: No general election opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Republican.

candidates.name: William Timmons
candidates.summary: William Timmons is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. He previously served in the South Carolina Senate and as an assistant solicitor (prosecutor) in Greenville County, and is a captain in the U.S. Air Force Judge Advocate General's Corps. Timmons has stated that this will be his final re-election campaign before retiring in 2028.

candidates.name: Courtney McClain
candidates.summary: Courtney McClain is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 4th Congressional District. A Spartanburg native, she is a civil rights activist and the first Black woman and Generation Z candidate to be a major-party nominee for this seat. McClain holds a BA from the University of South Carolina and an MA in Political Science from Howard University, and has served as President of the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast is based entirely on structural and contextual fundamentals. Cook Political Report rates the district Solid Republican. Incumbent William Timmons has held the seat since 2018 and won his June 9 primary with nearly 66% of the vote against two challengers, also securing President Trump's endorsement. The Democratic nominee, Courtney McClain, is a 25-year-old first-time candidate who advanced uncontested from her primary, and Libertarian Jessica Ethridge is also on the ballot. SC-04 (Greenville/Spartanburg counties) is a reliably Republican Upstate district where recent elections have produced Republican margins of roughly 30–40 points. Without any polling evidence of a shift in the general-election environment, Timmons remains an overwhelming favorite. Confidence is medium rather than high due to the complete absence of general-election polling.
